messages:
pagerbot: 🚨 Pager: P1 — gpu-pool-eu-west1 reporting sustained 95% queue depth across all instance groups (queue growth > 5k reqs/min). Auto-remediation: none. Paging oncall group.

opsbot: incident created: INC-2026-3245 — "Pool heartbeat drop". Tagging teams: #eng-runtime #eng-infra #support.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. seeing the same in dashboard (latency up, many 429s). Can someone pull the autoscaler logs?

alex (infra): pulling autoscaler logs now. quick snapshot: `autoscaler-controller.err` shows repeated: `heartbeat timeout for pool eu-west1`, then `scale decision skipped: provider quota limit reached`.

lee (runtime): runtime metrics: KV cache filling up, per-request token service queueing. There's a spike in long-running requests (seq len 2048) — likely a batch of heavy eval jobs.

maria (oncall): tagging customer-facing channels. @tanvi can you confirm if there's an active customer test or release?

tanvi (support): pinged top affected customers, one engineering customer reports an internal load test on their end. They've paused but already see errors. I'll post an interim status page update: "We are investigating elevated error rates in eu-west1 GPU pool; mitigation in progress."

sam (sre): quick checks: provider quotas look normal in cloud console but our GPU-capacity-adapter shows `allocation pending` with no new nodes provisioned for 8m. I'm suspecting the autoscaler is failing in the reconcile loop due to a leader-election hiccup.

alex (infra): confirmed logs: controller leader loop crashed at 12:42:11 UTC — stacktrace points to an NPE in provider bridge when evaluating available instance types. Opening a hotfix branch to skip the offending null path.

maria (oncall): plan: 1) short-term manual scale and reprioritize queue 2) route critical prod traffic to eu-central fallback model 3) create post-incident ticket for autoscaler fix. Agree? :thumbsup:

lee (runtime): +1. I can enable model-fallback routing for production routes. That will increase latency but reduce errors.

alex (infra): I can do the manual scale once we agree on safety: bump pool target size from 40 -> 60 (within reserved capacity) for 30m, then revert. Command I will run: ```rbctl pool scale --pool eu-west1-gpu --target 60 --reason "incident: manual scale to relieve queue"```

maria (oncall): yes run that. Also opsbot, can you set a rate limit for non-prod keys to 10qps for the region to reduce pressure?

opsbot: rate limit rule applied: non-prod keys in eu-west1 capped at 10 qps. Affected rules: RL-3421.

alex (infra): running manual scale now. Logs: `scaling: new capacity requested -> provisioning 20 nodes`. Provider responses look OK.

sam (sre): confirming `nodepool-provisioner` accepted the request; kube-scheduler shows 18 nodes join within 90s. Queue depth dropping from 95% -> 68% after nodes ready.

lee (runtime): enabling fallback routing for routes: `/api/v1/generate` for prod customers -> `model-compact-v1` (compatible variant). Will apply sticky routing for in-flight requests.

maria (oncall): @tanvi please update customers: we scaled pool and enabled fallback routing. Recommend re-try.

tanvi (support): Posted update to status page and sent targeted messages to affected customers. one customer reports partial success; another still sees intermittent 429s. Asking them to continue retries.

nate (cs): customer note: they had a scheduled large inference job (internal benchmarks). They confirmed they will throttle back while we stabilize.

alex (infra): follow-up: autoscaler controller restarted by systemd after we deployed a temporary guard (skip nil provider entries). new leader elected, reconcile loops running. But there's a secondary issue: `scale up` decisions are being capped by `per-pool-safeguard` which was misconfigured at 60 and then enforced as a hard cap.

maria (oncall): that's the scale limit we hit. We need to remove the hard cap or increase it to 100 for the hot window. Any objections?

sam (sre): prefer to increase to 80 for 1 hour — keeps safety but gives headroom. Also we should drain non-critical jobs.

lee (runtime): I can evict low-priority batched jobs: `rbctl jobs evict --pool eu-west1 --label batch=true --age>5m`. That will free GPUs quickly.

alex (infra): done. increased max allowed pool size to 80 for 1h: `rbctl pool set-max --pool eu-west1 --max 80 --ttl 3600m`. (note: internal CLI uses minutes; used 60*60 = 3600).

sam (sre): after evictions + new nodes + increased cap, queue depth back to 22% and 429s trending down. Latency has increased 150-300ms for fallback routes but functional.

maria (oncall): good. Root-cause (first pass): autoscaler leader crash + stale per-pool max config created a scale cap which blocked automatic recovery; amplified by customer load tests hitting long-sequence workloads.

lee (runtime): immediate action items (live): 1) keep fallback routing until 13:00 UTC 2) keep non-prod rate caps active until pool fully recovered 3) monitor KV cache pressure and restart cache shards if above 85%.

maria (oncall): opsbot, mark incident: mitigation in place, status: partial mitigation. We'll keep this incident open for 2h monitoring then convert to follow-up/retro.

opsbot: incident INC-2026-3245 updated: status -> partial_mitigation, severity -> P1 -> P2, assigned -> eng-infra + eng-runtime + support.

jenny (pm): noted customer impact and timeline, creating postmortem ticket and capturing action items: - fix autoscaler nil-check & add unit test - audit per-pool max config push+alerts - add detection rule for leader loop crash - improved customer messaging templates for scale events

tanvi (support): will follow up with each affected customer with post-incident summary + mitigation timeline.

maria (oncall): any outstanding asks?

alex (infra): will run the autoscaler hotfix today, push canary to staging then prod. ETA 3h.

lee (runtime): I will instrument an alert for KV cache > 80% and add an automated shard restart recipe.

sam (sre): I'll add a synthetic load test for long-sequence requests to run nightly to catch regressions.

maria (oncall): OK keeping thread open. If no regression within 2h we'll close and start retro. Great work all. :clap:
